newsitem.title: UK: U.K. jobless rate falls to lowest level in 6 years.
newsitem.headline: U.K. jobless rate falls to lowest level in 6 years.

text.p: Britain's jobless rate has fallen to its lowest level in six years, according to government statistics released Wednesday, the lowest total jobless figure since October 1990 and the 12th consecutive monthly fall.
Unemployment fell by 68,200 in February to 1.75 million, or 6.2 percent of the work force.
Prime Minister John Major, facing the prospect of defeat in elections on May 1, welcomed the jobless fall.
The economic data also showed unexpected strength in retail sales, which rose 0.5 percent in February, indicating a return of consumer confidence.
Average earnings rose by an unexpected 5.0 percent in January, the highest figure since November 1992.

That rise in earnings sent worrying signals that the British economy might be steaming ahead too quickly, putting pressure on interest rates -- currently at 6 percent -- for whichever government is elected in six weeks.

"The data are not strong enough to trigger a pre-election rate hike, but the jump in earnings will boost speculation that a post-election tightening could be as large as 50 basis points (half a percentage point)," said Bank of America economist Jeremy Hayward.
